title: Illustrator-gated slash commands and Gallery actions undocumented
reality: In 2.3.0 the /illustrate and /selfie slash commands and all image/video generation settings are hidden until the Illustrator package is installed, and the Connections 'Illustrator' defaults category was renamed 'Images'. Gallery generation controls (Illustrate, Selfie, Storyboard, Video, Animate, Background) now require Illustrator to be installed AND enabled for that chat in every mode; Game setup's 'Visual Generation' was renamed 'Illustrator' and its controls appear only when the package is installed. Automatic/Gallery selfie prompt generation also routes through the per-chat Prompt Model text connection (#3638).
fix: Add a short 'Slash commands are package-gated' note to custom-tools.md (near the Regex Scripts disambiguation section): /illustrate and /selfie only exist once the Illustrator agent package is installed; Gallery Illustrate/Selfie/Storyboard/Video/Animate/Background actions require Illustrator installed+enabled per chat (2.3.0); selfie prompts use the chat's selected Prompt Model connection (#3638).

title: Package-owned commands and no-restart activation missing
reality: 2.3.0 made command toggles package-owned: agent sections, settings, and package-owned command toggles appear in Chat Settings -> Agents only for agents actually installed; the six table games (UNO, Chess, Poker, 8-Ball Pool, Tic-Tac-Toe, Rock-Paper-Scissors) appear in the Commands controls without separate Add Agent entries; built-in Conversation commands stay configurable with no downloads. 2.3.2 (#3699) made installed Conversation games appear immediately in slash-command autocomplete and activate/deactivate their command and runtime contributions without an Engine restart (route-bearing packages keep a safe restart path).
fix: Add a subsection to custom-tools.md distinguishing three invocation surfaces: user-defined custom tools (this file), built-in engine tools, and package-owned commands contributed by installed agent packages (2.3.0); note table games surface as Commands toggles, and that installing a Conversation game activates its slash commands live without engine restart (#3699), while route-bearing packages require restart.

title: update_about_me entry lacks 2.3 built-in status and Professor Mari drafting
reality: 2.3.0 explicitly kept Conversation mode's About Me profile and the update_about_me tool built into the Engine — they are NOT downloadable agents — while most optional agent features moved to packages. 2.3.2 moved About Me AI-drafting from the per-editor 'AI Write' controls to Professor Mari: Character/Persona Convo editors no longer expose a separate model connection or source settings; Mari inspects the saved character/persona, writes the bio in their voice, and saves it directly to the real About Me field.
fix: In the Built-In Tools list entry for update_about_me in custom-tools.md, add: '(2.3.x) About Me and this tool remain engine built-ins, not downloadable agent packages; as of 2.3.2 About Me AI drafting is done through Professor Mari, not the removed per-editor AI Write controls.'

title: Built-in tools list predates 2.3 package split
reality: 2.3.0 moved Hierarchical Maps, Conversation calls, and all table games into optional downloadable packages with package-owned server runtimes, removing 25,000+ lines of optional agent/map/call/game code from the base Engine in favor of capability registries; Music DJ is a downloadable package and music player/Spotify controls show 'Download Music DJ Agent to configure' until it is installed. The skill's flat '~18 built-in tools' list (including the six spotify_* tools) implies everything is always present in the base engine.
fix: Annotate the Built-In Tools section in custom-tools.md: as of 2.3.0 the base engine exposes capability registries and several tool-bearing features (Maps, Calls, table games, music/Spotify via Music DJ) are supplied by downloadable agent packages, so their tools exist only when the package is installed; core tools like roll_dice, lorebook, chat-summary/variable tools, and update_about_me remain engine built-ins.

title: Connection Custom Parameters behavior undocumented
reality: 2.3.2 applied saved Connection Custom Parameters to every API-backed text generation that uses that connection — including Noodle and custom endpoints hosted locally — while preserving per-chat and per-call overrides; and (#3688) Custom Parameters now preserve arbitrary JSON values and convenient bare string values instead of discarding them as invalid drafts, and unified reasoning-effort requests were restored for dynamically discovered OpenRouter models.
fix: Add a note that saved Connection Custom Parameters apply to every API-backed text generation on that connection including Noodle and local custom endpoints (2.3.2), accept arbitrary JSON and bare string values (#3688), and are overridable per chat/call. Relevant to anyone wiring custom/local endpoints for tool-calling characters.

title: 2.3.x provider and env-var additions absent from skill
reality: 2.3.x connection/provider changes not reflected anywhere in the skill: Venice.ai added as an Image Generation service with live model discovery and native /image/generate support (2.3.2 #3682); persistent NovelAI V4.5 style plates with independent strength/fidelity and subject-count framing (2.3.3 #3725/#3726); bare Cohere API roots and versioned URLs now routed through Cohere's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (2.3.2); configurable pauses between generated TTS dialogue lines with a shared saved preference (2.3.3 #3718); new env vars CHAT_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS (slow Conversation/Roleplay/Game providers) and AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED=false (persistent launcher update opt-out, manual updates unaffected) (2.3.3 #3730).
fix: Add an env-var note to custom-tools.md covering CHAT_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS and AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED (#3730) alongside the existing CUSTOM_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS docs; route Venice.ai (#3682), NovelAI V4.5 style plates, Cohere OpenAI-compatible routing, and TTS dialogue-line pauses (#3718) to the architecture.md provider coverage.

title: No-marketplace claim ignores official Download Agents catalog
reality: extensions.md states 'There's no central marketplace yet. Distribution is manual.' Since 2.3.0 Marinara ships a full-page Agents -> Download Agents library backed by the official Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents catalog of individually verified first-party packages (29-package catalog, Writer/Tracker/Misc groupings, Install All/Uninstall All, mode-compatibility badges in 2.3.2 #3676, startup auto-update in 2.3.1, and per-major compatibility lanes in 2.3.3 #3712). Client CSS/JS extensions remain a separate, manually distributed surface — but the unqualified claim now reads as 'Marinara has no official package distribution', which is false and conflates the two surfaces.
fix: Rewrite the 'Installation and Distribution' opening in extensions.md: client extensions are still manually distributed (JSON/zip, no extension marketplace), BUT since v2.3.0 an official Agents -> Download Agents catalog of verified capability packages exists (Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents) — cross-reference it and state explicitly that downloadable agent packages are a different surface from client extensions.

title: Fork-the-engine advice superseded by capability packages
reality: extensions.md's 'What Extensions CAN'T Do' section ends with 'If you need any of these, fork the engine', and the 'When to Use' comparison lists only Extension/Custom Agent/Custom Tool/Character card/Lorebook. Since 2.3.0 downloadable capability packages supply exactly this class of functionality without forking: package-owned server runtimes and responsive client surfaces (Maps, Calls, table games), and capability API 1.3 (2.3.2 #3690) gives packages safe model routing, persistence, history/checkpoints, resources, logging, transactions, and client contribution loading; the Marinara-Agents repo has public contribution rules and review flow.
fix: In extensions.md, update 'What Extensions CAN'T Do' to point at downloadable agent/capability packages (capability API 1.3, #3690) as the supported path for server runtimes, new commands, and client surfaces before suggesting a fork, and add 'Downloadable agent package — packaged server runtime + client surface, distributed via the official catalog' as a row in the 'When to Use Extensions vs. Other Surfaces' list.
